question: The marked price of a ceiling fan is Rs. 4,200 and the shopkeeper allows a discount of 5% on it. If his profit is 14%, then the cost price of the fan is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Using the direct relation between Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP):

CP / MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%)

⇒ CP / 4200 = (100 − 5) / (100 + 14)

⇒ CP / 4200 = 95 / 114 = 5 / 6

⇒ CP = 4200 × 5 / 6 = 3500

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = Rs. 4200

Discount (D%) = 5%

Profit (P%) = 14%

CP = ?SPMP = 4200
• +14% Profit
• -5% DiscCP / MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%)
**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − D%) / 100

Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100 / (100 + P%)

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 4200 × (100 − 5) / 100

⇒ SP = 4200 × 95 / 100

⇒ SP = Rs. 3990

⇒ CP = 3990 × 100 / (100 + 14)

⇒ CP = 3990 × 100 / 114

⇒ CP = 35 × 100 = Rs. 3500

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP) & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price. Formula: SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100

Profit & Loss

Profit and Loss are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise. Formula: SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, then the equivalent single discount is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.
